completion.response_text: {"schema_version":"direct-filter/1.0","status":"ready","assumptions":["IPv4 traffic carried by TCP means packets that are both IPv4 and TCP.","TTL at most one means ip.ttl <= 1.","Expiring refers to a low TTL value indicating the packet is about to be dropped."],"clarifying_question":null,"missing_slots":[],"display_filter":"ip and tcp and ip.ttl <= 1"}

{"schema_version":"direct-filter/1.0","status":"ready","assumptions":["IPv4 datagrams carried by UDP are identified by the presence of both ip and udp protocol layers.","Expiring datagrams are interpreted as TTL no greater than 1, matching ip.ttl <= 1.","No specific source or destination constraints were requested beyond the directional interpretation already noted."],"clarifying_question":null,"missing_slots":[],"display_filter":"ip and udp and ip.ttl <= 1"}

{"schema_version":"direct-filter/1.0","status":"ready","assumptions":["ACK flag refers to tcp.flags.ack being set","Directional destination port uses tcp.dstport"],"clarifying_question":null,"missing_slots":[],"display_filter":"tcp.dstport == 443 && tcp.flags.ack"}

{"schema_version":"direct-filter/1.0","status":"ready","assumptions":["Interpret the request at packet scope over complete Ethernet/IPv4 packets.","Treat source and destination constraints as directional.","Acknowledged TCP segments means packets with the TCP ACK flag set.","Destination service port 443 refers to the TCP destination port."],"clarifying_question":null,"missing_slots":[],"display_filter":"tcp.flags.ack == 1 && tcp.dstport == 443"}

{"schema_version":"direct-filter/1.0","status":"ready","assumptions":["A record type is DNS type 1.","DNS queries are identified by the QR flag being 0 (query).","mDNS uses the same dns.qry.type field as standard DNS.","The dns protocol field matches both DNS and mDNS packets in Wireshark."],"clarifying_question":null,"missing_slots":[],"display_filter":"dns && dns.flags.response == 0 && dns.qry.type == 1"}

{"schema_version":"direct-filter/1.0","status":"ready","assumptions":["Request-side means DNS query messages (qr bit = 0).","IPv4 address records means queries for record type A (type value 1).","No transport limitation means no UDP/TCP filter is applied."],"clarifying_question":null,"missing_slots":[],"display_filter":"dns.flags.response == 0 && dns.qry.type == 1"}

{"schema_version":"direct-filter/1.0","status":"ready","assumptions":["FIN packets identified by tcp.flags.fin being set","DNS responses identified by dns.flags.response being set"],"clarifying_question":null,"missing_slots":[],"display_filter":"tcp.flags.fin == 1 || dns.flags.response == 1"}

{"schema_version":"direct-filter/1.0","status":"ready","assumptions":["TCP close segment carrying FIN is identified by tcp.flags.fin being set.","Response-side DNS message is identified by dns.flags.response being true.","The two conditions are combined with logical OR."],"clarifying_question":null,"missing_slots":[],"display_filter":"tcp.flags.fin || dns.flags.response"}

{"schema_version":"direct-filter/1.0","status":"ready","assumptions":["Interpret the request at packet scope over complete Ethernet/IPv4 packets.","Treat source and destination constraints as directional.","DNS over UDP is identified by the dns protocol filter.","IPv4 destination must be within the 10.0.0.0/8 private range."],"clarifying_question":null,"missing_slots":[],"display_filter":"udp and ip.dst == 10.0.0.0/8 and not dns"}

{"schema_version":"direct-filter/1.0","status":"ready","assumptions":["Interpret the request at packet scope over complete Ethernet/IPv4 packets.","Treat source and destination constraints as directional.","Private 10/8 means IPv4 destination in 10.0.0.0/8.","Not decoded as DNS means the DNS dissector did not attach to the packet, expressed as !dns.","UDP includes both source and destination UDP packets."],"clarifying_question":null,"missing_slots":[],"display_filter":"udp && ip.dst == 10.0.0.0/8 && !dns"}

{"schema_version":"direct-filter/1.0","status":"ready","assumptions":["ECN-enabled means the IP ECN field is nonzero, indicating either ECT(1), ECT(0), or CE is set.","TCP SYN packets are identified by the SYN flag being set.","TTL at most one means ip.ttl <= 1.","The two conditions are combined with logical OR."],"clarifying_question":null,"missing_slots":[],"display_filter":"(ip.dsfield.ecn > 0 && tcp.flags.syn == 1) || ip.ttl <= 1"}

{"schema_version":"direct-filter/1.0","status":"ready","assumptions":["Connection start interpreted as SYN packets (tcp.flags.syn==1).","ECE flag matched via tcp.flags.ece==1.","Expiring IPv4 traffic interpreted as ip.ttl<=1.","Both conditions combined with logical OR as the request says 'plus' between two distinct packet classes."],"clarifying_question":null,"missing_slots":[],"display_filter":"(tcp.flags.syn==1 && tcp.flags.ece==1) || ip.ttl<=1"}

{"schema_version":"direct-filter/1.0","status":"ready","assumptions":["DNS AAAA questions are identified by dns.qry.type == 28","DNS NXDOMAIN responses are identified by dns.flags.response == 1 and dns.flags.rcode == 3"],"clarifying_question":null,"missing_slots":[],"display_filter":"dns and (dns.qry.type == 28 or (dns.flags.response == 1 and dns.flags.rcode == 3))"}

{"schema_version":"direct-filter/1.0","status":"ready","assumptions":["Asks for IPv6 addresses means DNS queries with type AAAA (query type value 28).","Reports a name error means DNS response with rcode 3 (NXDOMAIN)."],"clarifying_question":null,"missing_slots":[],"display_filter":"dns and (dns.qry.type == 28 or dns.flags.response == 1 and dns.flags.rcode == 3)"}

{"schema_version":"direct-filter/1.0","status":"ready","assumptions":["Using tcp.flags.fin and tcp.flags.reset boolean fields from the catalog to match FIN or RST regardless of other flags set.","No port or direction restrictions applied."],"clarifying_question":null,"missing_slots":[],"display_filter":"tcp.flags.fin == 1 || tcp.flags.reset == 1"}

{"schema_version":"direct-filter/1.0","status":"ready","assumptions":["Request applies to TCP segments only.","No port or direction filtering needed per the request.","Segments with additional flags (ACK, ECE, etc.) are included.","tcp.flags.rst is the standard Wireshark field for the RST flag."],"clarifying_question":null,"missing_slots":[],"display_filter":"tcp.flags.rst || tcp.flags.fin"}

{"schema_version":"direct-filter/1.0","status":"ready","assumptions":["IPv4 TTL field is ip.ttl, a standard Wireshark field not listed in retrieved_fields.","UDP packets include any upper-layer protocol carried over UDP, such as DNS and mDNS.","TTL of 64 or higher means ip.ttl >= 64."],"clarifying_question":null,"missing_slots":[],"display_filter":"udp && ip.ttl >= 64"}

{"schema_version":"direct-filter/1.0","status":"ready","assumptions":["IPv4 TTL field is ip.ttl","UDP includes DNS and mDNS without port narrowing"],"clarifying_question":null,"missing_slots":[],"display_filter":"udp and ip.ttl >= 64"}

{"schema_version":"direct-filter/1.0","status":"ready","assumptions":["The request is for IP-layer destination addresses in 10.0.0.0/8, so standard Wireshark ip.dst fields are used rather than the retrieved protocol-specific fields.","Any protocol is included, so no protocol restriction is applied.","Only packets whose destination IP is within 10.0.0.0/8 qualify; source address is irrelevant to inclusion."],"clarifying_question":null,"missing_slots":[],"display_filter":"ip.dst == 10.0.0.0/8"}

{"schema_version":"direct-filter/1.0","status":"ready","assumptions":["dns.flags.response covers both DNS and mDNS response packets.","dns.flags.rcode is the standard Wireshark field for the DNS response code; NOERROR is 0.","Extended RCODEs (dns.resp.ext_rcode) are included implicitly because dns.flags.rcode reflects the full RCODE when EDNS is present."],"clarifying_question":null,"missing_slots":[],"display_filter":"(dns.flags.response == 1) && (dns.flags.rcode != 0)"}
